pain_points: Accounting rules are applied in three places
Two data paths reconciled by hand
Loan tags written back to the source systems

today.headline: Northwind applies accounting rules in three places and reconciles two data paths by hand before every close.
today.lede: Five source systems feed batch ETL, a legacy accounting engine and a SQL data warehouse. Posting rules live in all three, and month-end adjustments arrive as spreadsheets. This view is a hypothesis built from the stated inputs, not the client's own diagram.

so_what.text: Every rule change has to be made and tested three times, and the GL, the warehouse and securitization reporting can disagree by design. That is the main source of close effort and audit questions.
so_what.trade_off: Consolidating the rules means rebuilding logic that works today, so the proof of concept must show the hub reproduces legacy results before anything is retired.

systems.name: CardCore
systems.role: Card processor: accounts, purchases, payments and fees.
systems.issue: Sends the same transactions to ETL and the warehouse in two formats.

systems.name: LoanSys
systems.role: Loan servicing: originations, schedules and repayments.
systems.issue: Receives loan tags written back from the warehouse.

systems.name: Securitization servicer
systems.role: Pool and investor data for the securitized receivables.

systems.name: ETL jobs
systems.role: Nightly jobs that transform source files and derive journal lines.
systems.issue: Accounting rules embedded in transformation code, without versioning.

systems.name: Manual adjustment files
systems.role: Month-end adjustments keyed by the accounting team.
systems.issue: No maker-checker evidence in the system; lineage stops at the file.

systems.name: Reference data hub
systems.role: Reference capability: mastered product and organisation data.
systems.issue: Not in the stated landscape; product mappings appear to be held in code.

systems.name: Legacy accounting engine
systems.role: Applies posting rules and summarises journals for the GL.
systems.issue: Second copy of the posting rules; changes need a developer.

systems.name: ECL engine
systems.role: Calculates expected credit loss by account and stage.

systems.name: Data warehouse
systems.role: Reporting store for products, balances and securitization.
systems.issue: Third copy of accounting logic, used for non-GL reporting.

systems.name: BI reports
systems.role: Product and portfolio dashboards from the warehouse.

systems.name: Regulatory reporting
systems.role: Regulatory returns assembled from the warehouse and the GL.
systems.issue: Manual reconciliation between the warehouse and the GL each quarter.

principles.principle: Apply the accounting rules once, to the source transactions
principles.today: Rules run in the ETL jobs, the legacy engine and the warehouse.

principles.principle: Keep balances reconciled by design, with one golden source
principles.today: The GL and the warehouse are reconciled by hand; securitization reads the warehouse.

target.headline: One accounting hub on the data fabric applies the rules once and feeds Workday and OneStream from a single reconciled source.
target.lede: Sources land once through data contracts, are conformed into the Financial Information Model, and are accounted in the hub under versioned rules. The GL receives journals at the agreed grain, and every other consumer reads the same golden source.

so_what.text: Rules move from three code bases into one governed accounting matrix, and the warehouse-to-GL reconciliation disappears because both read the same journal lines.
so_what.trade_off: The hub needs data platform engineering and accounting rule ownership that Northwind does not staff today; the GL-native engine option needs less new skill but leaves non-GL reporting on a separate path.

ownership.component: Accounting hub rule engine (product to confirm)

fim.headline: A contract-grain information model lets the GL, risk and securitization read the same facts.
fim.lede: The Financial Information Model holds every contract once, with its parties, product, organisation, events, balances and risk measures, so accounting and reporting stop rebuilding them separately.

so_what.text: Analytical attributes such as ECL stage, vintage and investor code stay in the model instead of becoming GL segments, which keeps the chart of accounts small.
so_what.trade_off: A contract-grain model is a larger data design effort up front than mapping file to file.

maf.headline: The Master Accounting Flow for merchant cards covers 17 events, proven before instalment loans reuse the same method.
maf.lede: Each product is walked from onboarding to close. Every event names its trigger, its balanced journal, the controls that apply and the attributes kept but not posted. Event counts are a draft until validated with Product and Finance.

so_what.text: 9 events are manual today and 4 exception paths are modelled explicitly, which is where the close effort and the audit findings concentrate.
so_what.trade_off: Modelling every event, including exceptions, takes workshop time from Product and Finance before any build starts.

products.name: Merchant credit cards
open_items: Rewards accrual treatment not yet agreed
Foreign-currency purchases excluded from the proof of concept

events.name: Account opened
events.trigger: New account record (account id, product, limit)

events.name: Annual fee charged
events.route: Hub sub-ledger, summarised daily to Workday by account and cost centre.
events.treatment: Fee income recognised over the fee period [to confirm]

events.name: Purchase posted
events.trigger: Authorised and settled purchase (txn id, amount, merchant)

events.name: Duplicate purchase file rejected
events.trigger: Second file with the same batch id and hash
events.route: Rejected at ingest and logged; no journal.

events.name: Interest accrued
events.dates: Effective: accrual date; accounting: open period
events.treatment: Effective interest on the drawn balance

events.name: Payment reversed (returned)
events.trigger: Return record linked to the original payment id
events.route: Hub sub-ledger; reversal linked to the original line.
events.reversal: Full reversal of the original payment lines, linked by payment id

events.name: Fee waiver
events.route: Governed adjustment in the hub with maker-checker.

events.name: Back-dated dispute credit
events.trigger: Dispute record with an effective date in a closed period
events.route: Hub sub-ledger in the open period, effective date kept.
events.dates: Effective: dispute date (closed period); accounting: current open period
events.treatment: Credit the receivable in the open period

events.name: Stage 1 to stage 2 transfer
events.trigger: ECL engine stage change (account id, stage)
events.route: FIM risk measure updated; no journal.
events.treatment: No accounting entry; drives the allowance

events.name: ECL allowance top-up
events.handled_today: Manual journal from the ECL engine
events.variant: All entities; IFRS 9 primary, US GAAP delta
events.route: Hub sub-ledger per ledger, summarised monthly.
events.treatment: IFRS 9 stage-based allowance; CECL lifetime difference in the delta ledger [to confirm]

events.name: Recovery received
events.trigger: Recovery payment on a charged-off account
events.treatment: Recovery recognised in profit or loss

events.name: Receivables sold to trust
events.trigger: Monthly pool cut (pool id, accounts, amount)
events.route: Hub sub-ledger; investor code kept in the FIM.
events.treatment: Derecognition depends on the trust structure [to confirm]

events.name: Account closed
events.route: FIM contract status updated; no journal.

events.name: Origination fee deferred
events.treatment: Deferred and amortised through effective interest

events.name: Late file re-run
events.trigger: Payment file received after the cut-off and re-run
events.route: Replayed events matched to originals; no new journal.
events.treatment: No duplicate entry; late events post to the open period

events.name: Payment holiday granted
events.route: FIM schedule updated; modification gain or loss assessed [to confirm].

migration.headline: A proof of concept on merchant cards, then three waves and a four-stage parallel run, retires the legacy rules safely.
migration.lede: Each wave runs in shadow and parallel against the legacy results before cutover. Durations, thresholds and savings stay to be sized until the proof of concept gives a baseline.

so_what.text: The parallel run turns retirement of three code bases into a measured decision: each component is switched off only when its exit thresholds hold.
so_what.trade_off: Running legacy and hub side by side doubles the run effort for the parallel period.

waves.name: Proof of concept: merchant cards
waves.scope: CardCore events through the hub to a Workday test tenant, with drill-back.
waves.exit: Hub reproduces one month of legacy card journals within the agreed thresholds.

waves.name: Cards and payments
waves.scope: CardCore and the payments switch in production shadow and parallel.
waves.exit: Two closes inside the exit thresholds.

waves.name: Instalment loans
waves.scope: LoanSys events reusing the card method.
waves.exit: Two closes inside the exit thresholds.

waves.name: Collections, ECL and securitization
waves.scope: Collections, ECL results and securitization reporting from the golden source.
waves.exit: Investor and regulatory reports agree to the GL by design.

waves.name: Decommission
waves.scope: Retire the ETL posting logic, the legacy engine and the warehouse accounting.
waves.exit: Legacy jobs off and archived; run cost released.

legacy.target: OneStream, repointed to the hub drill-back

confirm.item: Confirm the current-state landscape with Northwind's architecture team; this view is a hypothesis.
Choose the accounting hub rule engine product and the data platform.
Agree the securitization derecognition treatment and the rewards accrual policy.
Agree the GL posting grain with Finance and Technology.
Obtain the run-cost baseline before any saving is shown.
